name: The Harvard Route
text: [overview] Cross the bergschrund, climb five rope lengths of 50 degree ice, then the Spiral (first pitch about M6, with suspect blocks), a 5.9 chimney and M4 mixed to a bivy spot below the Nose (C1, 80 ft).
[overview] The 50 degree icefield leads to a ridge crest with a huge cornice over a 5000 ft drop.
[watch_out] Beyond the ridge, a massive cornice hangs over a 5000 foot drop toward the West Fork of the Ruth..
[approach] Parties camp on the glacier at the foot of Mt.
[approach] Cross the lower glacier, where crevasse navigation is needed, to the bergschrund that guards the Access Couloir at the foot of the face;
[descent_text] Cross the bergschrund at the bottom and return to the upper basin above camp, taking care among large crevasses.

name: Mt. Michelson, South Face
text: [overview] The southern side departs from the glacier of that name, covers 1000-2000' of loose blocks, talus and snow, and then follows a final line of snow and ice up to the crest of the summit ridge.
[detailed_rack] A few pickets and ice screws may help.

name: Standard Route
text: [overview] Regal feeds the 7,000 ft Stairway Icefall.
[overview] The route mostly follows low-angle glaciers well suited to ski travel.
[overview] Above that, the final pyramid has about 1,800 ft of steep technical ground of ice and snow, reached via its South East Ridge.
[detailed_rack] Snow pickets, a few ice screws, and standard glacier-expedition equipment.
[approach] The mountain is reached by ski-plane to the Nabesna Glacier in the Wrangell Mountains.

[approach] From the landing area, the route follows low-angle glaciers, with camps possible nearly anywhere along them, to the foot of the summit pyramid, which is steep technical ice and snow climbed by its southeast ridge.

name: Sheep Glacier
text: [approach] Access is normally by ski-plane onto the lower Sheep Glacier, though a very long walk in from the highway is possible.
[approach] From the landing, parties rope up and haul sleds up the glacier to a base camp.
[approach] The route climbs a glacial ramp through large crevasse fields and a tricky icefall.
[descent_text] The descent retraces the route down the glacier to the landing area, with the crevasse fields and icefall to negotiate again on the way down.

name: Col of the Wild
text: [overview] brief cruxes of ice or mixed rock appear now and then, with much simulclimbing on steep snow.
[overview] Near the top a large cornice may need tunneling.
[detailed_rack] Standard alpine rack: some small and medium cams, a nut selection, knifeblades, angles, screws for ice, specters and a few pickets.

name: New Mother Nature
text: [approach] The Gargoyle is a west-facing granite wall at the north entrance of the Ruth Gorge, on the east side of the glacier directly across from Mount Barille.
[approach] The base is reached over the Ruth Glacier, best done on skis, and how easy the crossing is depends on the state of the glacier.

name: North Face
text: [overview] Cross a bergschrund after moderate snow to reach the rock.

name: North Troll Couloir
text: [overview] Climb the 60 degree snow couloir, steep and west facing, between the North and Middle Trolls, up to the point right under the col.
[detailed_rack] A standard rack plus snow gear.

name: Northeast Ridge
text: [approach] Approach North Troll via the glacier from the landing strip.

name: Northwest Ridge
text: [approach] Little Switzerland is reached by flying to the Pika Glacier, where the base camp sits.

name: Kissing up the choss pile
text: [approach] From the Reed Lakes lot, walk to the former building site, short of Nugget Boulder and the Snowbird slab.
[approach] Then take the path bearing left up the drainage, past the Snowbird mine on your right, and keep going up the bowls to the pass.
[approach] The Snowbird Glacier lies below the pass, and the Nunatak is the small formation beside it.

name: Thunderbolt (Lightening Bolt) Couloir
text: [overview] Steep snow couloir, also a steep to extreme Chugach Front Range ski line, harder than Ptarmigan North.
[what_to_bring] crampons — advisable (boot and ski).
[what_to_bring] ice axe or ice tool — or at least a whippet

name: Crystal Cave couloir
text: [overview] A 50-55 degree face of ice and snow gives way to an 800' ice couloir ending at a bivy in an ice cave formed naturally.
[overview] 800' of mixed ground, ice and snow then lead to the delicate, corniced SW ridge and the summit.
[approach] Peak 11,300 lies beside the West Fork of the Ruth Glacier, a little north of Mt.
[approach] The route starts on a steep snow and ice face that leads into an ice couloir, with a natural ice cave near the top of the couloir.

name: Right Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] Rock protection from .3 to 1, ice screws, and possibly a picket.
[approach] Peak 11,300 lies beside the West Fork of the Ruth Glacier, a little north of Mt.
[approach] The couloir is on the west face, a short ski up the glacier beyond the southwest ridge.

name: Southwest Ridge
text: [overview] Climb the southwest ridge by weaving between snow slopes and exposed, crumbly scree, choosing the easiest line.
[overview] Higher up, past the rock band, the ridge becomes a fairly gentle snow slope to the pointed summit.
[detailed_rack] Ice screws and pickets could add security if required.
[what_to_bring] crevasse-rescue kit — prudent, especially for the lower-glacier approach
[approach] The lower approach crosses glaciated ground, so rope up and carry crevasse rescue gear.
[approach] The route starts from the small pocket northeast of Crosson and follows the southwest ridge, picking the easiest line between loose scree and snow slopes.

name: Mixed Inhibitions
text: [overview] P2 (M7, 25 m) climbs a very steep crack that trends left in a corner facing left, then neve and a runnel to a snow ledge.
[approach] the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark.

name: S (north) couloir, The
text: [detailed_rack] Snow pickets, or a running belay if judged necessary.

name: Ski Tracks
text: [overview] the first moves from the snowfield have sparse gear and a fall would be bad.
[overview] Steep snow and a sheet of thick-or-thin ice lead right to fixed anchors.
[detailed_rack] Small to medium cams, a set of nuts, half a dozen screws for ice, a handful of specters, and optionally a picket or two.
[approach] the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark.
[approach] Ski Tracks lies right of the main snow gully and right of the Hookers line.

name: Pure Retro
text: [overview] Steep ice and snow lead up to splitter cracks and flakes on the west pillar.

name: It's Included
text: [detailed_rack] more wires, cord and pitons help if rappel anchors lie under snow or are in poor shape.

name: Standard Route (North Side)
text: [overview] Glacier travel and steep snow reaching roughly 35-40 degrees.
[detailed_rack] Pickets and glacier travel gear.

name: North Face
text: [overview] A base camp near 8,000 ft sits in a crevasse maze offering some shelter from big avalanches off Ahtna Peak.
[overview] Serac fall threatens the North Face, where steep snow alternates with one or two ice stretches at 40-55 degrees.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, screws for ice, and standard glacier-expedition equipment.
[approach] Access is by ski-plane to the Nabesna Glacier.
[approach] A base camp can be set among crevasses that give some protection from avalanches off the neighbouring peak, and a higher camp can go on the saddle that links Ahtna with Rime Peak.
[approach] Expect steep snow on the north face broken by a short band or two of alpine ice, and falling ice from seracs is a hazard.

name: Everywhere's a route!
text: [overview] Glacier ice here gives many summer options for toprope or lead, and since it is glacier ice it changes continually.

name: The Friends Along the Way
text: [overview] A couloir with over 2500 feet of gain, with snow close to vertical and traverses over chossy rock sections.
[overview] The first fork: steep snow if you go right, then 50 feet of steep choss;
[overview] going left means far steeper snow and some snow bridges.
[detailed_rack] A rope and a skeleton rack are worth carrying if snow anchors for descending are within your skills.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — required

name: Northeast Face
text: [overview] Takes the steepest part of the northeast face, rising from an unofficially named glacier called Scott, at the top of Denali's Unit 10.
[overview] Expect 50 degree steep snow combined with 70 degree alpine ice.
[overview] The crux is the last move, where a cornice must be crossed to reach the summit.
[detailed_rack] Screws and pickets.

name: Sunset Glacier
text: [overview] Ascend the Sunset Glacier into its higher basin and bear onto the shorter southwest fork, mindful of crevasses, to the col under the south ridge.
[overview] Snow steepens to the north, then a small basin lies east (watch for large cracks as summer goes on), then a short headwall, the crux, to the southeast ridge.
[overview] a large bergschrund leads some parties to pitch this short section.
[overview] Follow the ridge up, watch for cornices on the northeast side and avalanche hazard to the south.
[detailed_rack] Basic glacier travel kit: ice axe, crampons, pickets and so on.
[approach] Scott Peak rises steeply above the head of the Sunset Glacier.

[approach] Parties reach the Thorofare River gravel bar from the Eielson Visitor Center area on the park road (check current road and bus status), then follow the river toward the Sunset Glacier basin, which needs a river crossing that can be difficult on warm days and a
[approach] Once on the Sunset Glacier, the route follows it to its upper basin.

name: Smaug's Hoard
text: [approach] Fly to the Pika Glacier and ski to the foot of The Throne's south face.
[approach] The first pitch starts at the snow apex on the left edge of the face;
[descent_text] From the top, the party descends the west face of The Throne by a series of rappels down a drainage that carries running water, with large bergschrunds to cross lower down.

name: Smoke em' if you got em'
text: [overview] Pitches 1-3 are the couloir (simul-climbing is possible depending on snow quality);
[detailed_rack] 3-6 snow pickets, cams from .5 to #2, and a full set of nuts.

name: Solva Buttress
text: [overview] Stash crampons, axes and boots near the bergschrund, and leave something bright and large some distance from the rock, aligned with the exit, so the spot can be spotted from high above on the descent.
[overview] A chossy gully, reached up the triangular snow patch beside the 4th tower's left flank, leads to the start.

name: South Buttress
text: [overview] Cross the schrund where possible, then 5th and 4th class terrain leads to a big corner facing left;
[overview] Descend via the western ridge, rappelling the gully or its skier's-left face to the triangle snowfield, then the gully at its lower left edge to the glacier.

name: South Face Couloir
text: [overview] Climb the broad snow couloir splitting the Throne's south face (7390 feet).

name: South Ridge
text: [overview] A ski-mountaineering classic that crosses an ice fall, which may be the crux of the day: a 35-40 degree slope of snow or ice where seracs and crevasses determine if the left or right side is better.
[overview] Cross the 27 Mile Glacier to reach the saddle between Sapphire and Gendarme 5,570, on a 30-40 degree slope;
[overview] a large bergschrund may open there in summer or early in the season and can be skirted by a class 4 rib on the left.
[overview] From the saddle, climb the 5th class, corniced south ridge.
[detailed_rack] Glacier gear: some pickets, crampons, ice axe.

name: South Ridge
text: [overview] Climb snow to the col between South Troll and the chossy knob south of it, then follow the ridge for 120 m of fourth and low fifth class to a prominent tower.
[overview] For the summit, go 40 m up and left, beyond a rap station, to a gully's flakes, then about 45 m up past a big chockstone to a bowl possibly snowy.

name: South Tooth
text: [overview] A 5.5 climb on the prominent tooth, a sub-peak south of Sapphire, on the left when seen from the glacier bowl.
[overview] Ascend the basin called Catchers Mitt, then enter the higher part of the 27-Mile Glacier's bowl.

name: South West Ridge
text: [watch_out] Exposed corniced terrain along the crest requires constant care..
[watch_out] Heavily crevassed ground lies on the way back to camp..
[gear] Pickets.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, 4-6 ice screws and rock protection suited to alpine terrain.
[pro_needs] Rock and snow protection covers nearly everything;
[descent_text] It mixes downclimbing of moderate snow with rappels on the wide rocky crest, then threads a crevassed basin back to camp.

name: We Fear Change
text: [overview] Seven pitches, 700' of snow.
[overview] Easier snow or mixed ground in a gully leads to a mixed slab of 30' on its left;
[overview] A 150' leftward traverse across snow ledges reaches a stance by the ice gully, then three ice tiers: an M4 traverse onto thin ice, mixed and thin ice, and a WI4 column.
[overview] Then 600' of gully snow, steeper and narrower above;
[overview] Step right into a mixed dihedral with tricky gear, then a rock step and steep snow gain the ridge, and 3rd class ground (200') the summit.

name: Southeast Face
text: [detailed_rack] Bring snow protection as well as rock protection.

name: Southeast Face
text: [overview] A class-4 ridge of rock and snow leads to the foot of the southeast rock face, which is prominent.

name: Southwest Face
text: [overview] Snow climb with two short rock cruxes, depending on conditions.
[overview] A subtle weakness or couloir leads from the glacier onto a snow slope, and from there to the higher snow above.
[detailed_rack] Some medium cams for the upper part, crampons, ice axe, perhaps one or two pickets, and webbing for rappel anchors.

name: Southwest Face
text: [overview] Reach a large platform at the base by climbing the gully on the right side of the main corner (often snowy fourth class and low fifth class);

name: Southwest Ridge
text: [overview] Easy-to-moderate snow and a small 'shrund or moat crossing lead to the lowest band of rock.
[overview] this one trends up the western band of rock, though the snowfield or a different rock section would also work.
[overview] After reaching the ridge, a short snowfield must be crossed.
[detailed_rack] a picket is useful for the bergshrund.

name: Spam and Legs
text: [overview] Ascends the left-hand Royal Tower, as viewed from Pika Glacier.
[approach] From the airstrip and base camp on the Pika Glacier, ski or snowshoe west to the foot of the Royal Tower.
[approach] Depending on the line you may need an ice axe and crampons for steep snow and a bergschrund crossing.

name: Splitter Choss
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — optional for the approach

name: Bathtime with Toaster
text: [approach] The wall is in Suicide Basin and is reached either on foot via the West Glacier trail and across the Mendenhall Glacier, or by a short helicopter ride from Juneau.
[approach] The Suicide icefall is to the left of the route, and a big gentle slope lies higher up.

name: Infinite Jester
text: [approach] The wall is in Suicide Basin and is reached either on foot via the West Glacier trail and across the Mendenhall Glacier, or by a short helicopter ride from Juneau.

name: Path of the Fallen
text: [overview] Hurry beneath the serac that hangs over Suicide Wall, then climb or solo one WI3 pitch to a tiny hanging snowfield.
[approach] The wall is in Suicide Basin and is reached either on foot via the West Glacier trail and across the Mendenhall Glacier, or by a short helicopter ride from Juneau.
[approach] The approach passes beneath the Suicide icefall, so move quickly there.

name: The Chase
text: [approach] Little Switzerland is reached by flying to the Pika Glacier airstrip, which also serves as base camp.
[approach] From camp, ski or snowshoe west to the foot of the Royal Tower.
[approach] Depending on the line and conditions, an ice axe and crampons are likely needed for the steep snow slopes and the bergschrund at the base.

name: The Jester
text: [overview] Cross 40 degree snow and a bergschrund, then easy 5th class scrambling leads to a ledge with a 3/8" bolt.

name: The Lost Marsupial
text: [overview] The summit ridge is different terrain: boots, pickets and an ice axe may be required depending on snow, and it can be corniced.
[detailed_rack] Snowy conditions call for a picket or two on the corniced summit ridge.

name: The Middle Finger
text: [overview] The biggest of three spires in the gap over the Carmack glacier.
[overview] Reaching the spires needs glacier travel skills, as crevasses were snow covered.
[detailed_rack] Crampons and an axe or tools are needed for the approach;
[detailed_rack] a snow anchor may help.

name: Big Arapiles
text: [overview] Snow and rock mix, over broken ledges to a boulder on the summit ridge.
[overview] A rappel anchor on the boulder drops to the snow bench, and a second one above the gully returns to the skis or snowshoes left at the approach.
[approach] The Munchkin sits in the middle of Little Switzerland and is a short ski from the base camp on the Pika Glacier.
[approach] The route faces generally south and is mixed snow and rock with broken ledges up to a boulder on the summit ridge.
[descent_text] Descend by rappel: one anchor on a boulder drops you to the snow bench, and a second anchor above the gully gets you back down to where skis or snowshoes were left.

name: Royal Flush
text: [approach] From the airstrip and base camp on the Pika Glacier, ski or snowshoe west to the foot of the Royal Tower.
[approach] Depending on the line you may need an ice axe and crampons for steep snow and a bergschrund crossing.

name: The Sixth Sense - Sixth Tower
text: [overview] P1: cross a tiny ice bridge from the glacier to ledges (5.7), 60 ft.
[overview] Descend by rappels east of the last pitch, then more rappels back to the glacier, including a 200 ft one.

name: Oxidado Express
text: [overview] Easy unprotected face climbing leads to a moderate crack and a big ledge, 70m off the snow.
[approach] Little Switzerland on the Pika Glacier in Denali National Park is reached by air taxi from Talkeetna, and the approach from Pika base camp to The Throne is very short.

[approach] The route climbs the formation's west face, just left of a roof coated in vivid green lichen, starting off snow onto an easy unprotected face leading to a moderate crack system and a large ledge, before merging into the northwest ridge near the formation's mid
[descent_text] From the west summit, the way off is The Lost Marsupial (5.8), which runs down the formation's southern flank to the glacier and base camp.

name: Central Couloir
text: [overview] A snow climb best after rain, a slide and a refreeze.
[overview] Several steps of steeper snow and ice are separated by gentler ground;
[overview] Avoid it when the snowpack is unstable.
[detailed_rack] Pickets and ice screws, with alders for anchors.

name: North Gully
text: [overview] Turning right gives the main gully, snow with WI2 steps to the top;
[overview] Descent options: by way of Thunder-East Glacier, steep creek, or downclimbing or rappelling the gully.
[detailed_rack] Ice screws, and perhaps a picket or two.

name: Two Thumbs Up
text: [overview] The crux is a splitter crack just off the glacier.
[overview] Crampons are needed to cross the Lemmon glacier;
[overview] a mid-September ascent met no bergschrund trouble.

name: Freezy Nuts
text: [overview] snow and ice dominate, though easy mixed ground may appear in the narrows depending on conditions.
[overview] Higher up it widens, and a bit of cornice is likely just below the col.
[detailed_rack] Stoppers, cams in the .3 to 1 BD range, ice screws, possibly a picket.
[approach] Watch for crevasses near the end.

name: West Face
text: [overview] Cross moderate snow and a bergschrund.

name: West Ridge
text: [detailed_rack] Cams to #2 BD, 1-2 ice screws, plus crampons, an ice axe and glacier equipment.

name: West Ridge
text: [descent_text] From the summit, put on crampons and descend west on snow or ice until the scree slopes leading toward Twincicle Pass appear.
[descent_text] Go down through Twincicle Pass and the Twincicle Valley, which is a tangle of alders, and cross the short but very steep Twincicle Glacier.

name: West Ridge
text: [overview] Expect cornices, crevasses, serac hazard, glacier travel and tricky route finding.
[detailed_rack] Cams to 2 in, four to six nuts and ice screws, two or three pickets, cord to back up, replace or build rappel anchors, a pair of technical tools per climber, and a 60 m or 70 m rope.

name: West Twincil
text: [overview] alternatively stop above and climb a near-vertical snow step 10-20 ft tall to a ledge, from which a wider couloir continues to the basin below.
[detailed_rack] Steep snow and complex avalanche terrain;
[detailed_rack] consult snow and avalanche forecasts beforehand.
[approach] The line is steep, narrow and avalanche-prone, so it is best entered in very stable conditions after studying the map and the snow.

name: South West Ridge
text: [overview] Walk up the Castner Glacier, which is covered in rock, to the point where the south branch, M'Ladies Branch, splits away.
[detailed_rack] Some parties carry deadmen or snow pickets for protection, though not all do.
